title: Signal vs Accidentals: Personal KPI Lab Notebook
content:
Purpose
---
Scratch notebook to reduce ‘accidental work’ and increase measurable signal toward my quarterly objectives. Use this as a weekly running log, experiment tracker, and measurement spec. Not polished — brain dump + quick checks.

Motivation
---
I keep getting pulled into low-leverage activities (meeting fallout, adhoc reviews, status-checks) that inflate 'busy' time while starving focused work. If I treat my calendar & inbox as a noisy channel, I want to quantify signal-to-accidentals and run small experiments to shift the ratio.

Definitions (working)
---
- Signal: Work that directly maps to a chosen objective / key result and moves it measurably. Examples: shipping a rollout change, writing an eval, launching a PR that reduces cost.
- Accidentals: Context switches, reactive tickets not owned, meetings without clear outcomes, administrative follow-ups, and exploratory interruptions.
- Attention budget: Daily hours I can allocate to Signal. Aim = 4h deep-focus windows on weekdays.

Proposed metrics (simple, instrumentable)
---
1) Signal Share (%) = minutes tagged as Signal / total tracked work minutes. Goal: increase from baseline 42% -> 65% over 8 weeks.
2) Focus Hours/week = summed distraction-free hours (calendar blocks + RescueTime productive). Target: 20/week.
3) Accidental Events/week = count of unplanned interrupts >10m that blocked flow. Target: <= 6/week.
4) Delivered micro-outcomes/week = shipped changes that align to OKR (count). Target: 2/week.

Baseline (last 4 weeks rough numbers)
---
- Signal Share: ~42% (manual sample of 5 days)
- Focus Hours/week: 13–16
- Accidental Events/week: 9–12
- Delivered micro-outcomes/week: 0–1
Notes: manual tagging inconsistent; need a light-weight logging approach.

Measurement plan (minimal friction)
---
- Calendar: label blocks with prefix [S] or [A] (Signal/Accidental) using colors. Use 2-min daily quick review to adjust labels.
- RescueTime / Toggl: run in background for 4 weeks to correlate app-level focus with self-tags.
- Daily 3-line check-in (morning): top-1, blockers, expected 2h focus windows. Log in a single line in this doc.
- Weekly retro: copy 5 quick highlights here and compute metrics.

Hypotheses & experiments (two-week boxes)
---
H1: Setting a 10:00–12:00 no-meeting block increases Signal Share by ~15pp.
- Experiment: enforce block, push recurring meeting invites to afternoons, quick slack auto-replies for mornings.
- Measurement: compare Signal Share pre/post and focus hours.

H2: Batching adhoc reviews into two daily review windows reduces Accidental Events by 40%.
- Experiment: create /ad-hoc channel policy and link a PR triage doc; set review windows 11:00 and 16:00.

H3: A single weekly 30-min async status note replaces 1 recurring 1:1 and frees time for a micro-outcome.

Weekly check-in template (copy into weekly entries)
---
Week of YYYY-MM-DD
- Top focus (OKR):
- Signal Share (est):
- Focus Hours:
- Accidental Events:
- Shipped micro-outcomes:
- Quick notes / blockers:
- Adjustments for next week:

Retro notes (quick, messy)
---
- 2026-02-16: tried 10–12 block, got partial success; calendar pushback from infra team. Need to pre-announce and offer 1 backup slot.
- 2026-02-24: batched reviews into 11:00 & 16:00 slots — felt less fragmented, Accidental Events down to ~7.

Quick wins to try this week
---
- Add [S]/[A] prefixes to calendar and color-code.
- Auto-reply slack mornings with: "In focus window until 12:00 — DM for urgent, otherwise ping 14:30."
- Block 2x 90m focus windows Tues/Thurs in calendar; mark private.

Open questions / things to validate
---
- How to measure context-switch cost (tokens/minute? approximate lost time)? Manual probe idea: time-to-resume test (start timer after interruption).
- What’s the right cadence to report personal metrics to manager? weekly digest or biweekly? Prefer weekly note but keep short.
- If adoption fails because of org expectations, fallback = set one personal deep-focus day per week.

TODOS (actionable)
---
- [ ] Add calendar prefixes and color legend (today)
- [ ] Setup RescueTime & invite Jordan to shared dashboard (this week)
- [ ] Draft a one-paragraph heads-up to infra & product about focus windows and alternate slots (send Fri)
- [ ] Instrument 2-week measurement and share first snapshot in 2 weeks

Notes to self
---
- Be forgiving — this is an experiment. Data fidelity will be noisy; focus on directional signal.
- Keep logging habit: 2 minutes per day beats a perfect tracker that never gets used.

Scratch: quick sample weekly entry (copyable)
---
Week of 2026-03-02
- Top focus (OKR): Reduce inference cost per request by 8% through batching tweaks
- Signal Share (est): 58%
- Focus Hours: 18
- Accidental Events: 5
- Shipped micro-outcomes: 2 (batch-config change, rollback test)
- Quick notes / blockers: meeting drift on Wed; rescheduled.

End of notebook — keep iterating.
summary: Personal scratchpad for increasing signal-to-noise in daily work. Contains definitions, metrics, baseline, measurement plan, hypotheses, experiments, weekly template, retro notes, and todos.
